acts.desc: Host Ira Glass lays out the premise of this week's show.
acts.label: Prologue
Act One
acts.desc: A story that takes place at the crossroads where art meets commerce—a place where we can ask the question: Is the art of commerce better than the art of art? Writer (and occasional screenwriter) Sandra Tsing Loh accompanies a Hollywood screenwriter as he tries to sell a movie idea—a comedy in the style of Liar Liar.
acts.title: How To Talk Your Way Into A Half Million Dollars ... In 45 Minutes.

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: Writer/performer Danny Hoch performs a monologue taken from his one man show, Jails, Hospitals and Hip-Hop. It's a story about a guy who's been locked up for doing the most American activity possible: Selling stuff on the street (in this case Bart Simpson/O.J. Simpson t-shirts). His show is available on CD from his website.
acts.title: Jail Sell

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: Becoming a salesman can make you more confident and happy, make you ignore it when someone tells you "no"...and why that might be a bad thing. The story of a man who sold radio advertising.
acts.title: Who's The Man?

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc: What happens to you if you stay in sales all your life? 76-year-old salesman "Diamond" Jimmy Roy has sold everything from used cars to antiques to jewelery. Independent producer Dan Collison shadowed Jimmy Roy in his native Braddock, Pennsylvania, to talk to him about the philosophy that's kept him going as a salesman for over fifty years.
acts.title: The Secret To Being Rich And Happy
